schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE EMPLOYEE (
    EMPID INT,
    NAME VARCHAR(255),
    SUPERVISOR INT,
    SALARY INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (EMPID),
    CHECK (EMPID <> SUPERVISOR),
    CHECK (SALARY >= 0)
);

CREATE TABLE BONUS (
    EMPID INT,
    BONUS INT,
    PRIMARY KEY (EMPID),
    FOREIGN KEY (EMPID) REFERENCES EMPLOYEE(EMPID),
    CHECK (BONUS >= 0)
);
q1: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE BONUS < 1000 OR BONUS IS NULL
q2: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE COALESCE(BONUS,0) <1000
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE BONUS < 1000 OR BONUS IS NULL
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT EMPLOYEE.NAME, BONUS.BONUS FROM EMPLOYEE LEFT JOIN BONUS ON EMPLOYEE.EMPID = BONUS.EMPID WHERE COALESCE(BONUS,0) <1000
counterexample: INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (EMPID, NAME, SUPERVISOR, SALARY) VALUES (1, 'Alice', 2, 50000); INSERT INTO EMPLOYEE (EMPID, NAME, SUPERVISOR, SALARY) VALUES (2, 'Bob', 1, 60000); INSERT INTO BONUS (EMPID, BONUS) VALUES (1, 1500);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent. Q1 returns rows where BONUS < 1000 OR BONUS IS NULL, effectively including all employees who have no bonus or a bonus less than 1000. Q2 uses COALESCE(BONUS, 0) < 1000, which converts NULL to 0 and then compares, thus excluding employees with no bonus. This difference leads to different results.
counterexample_dsp: Create a test database with one employee who has no bonus (NULL) and another employee with a bonus of 1500. Q1 will return the employee with no bonus, while Q2 will not.
